q: Motoring at night you see these lights on a steady bearing, closing. What vessel is it and what do you do?
answer: A power-driven vessel crossing from your starboard — give way, turn to starboard
why: Red sidelight with a masthead light above: a power vessel showing you her port side.

figure.note: Night · bearing 045° relative, steady

q: At night you see a white light flashing six times then one long flash. What is it and where do you pass?
answer: A south cardinal — pass south of it
why: Clock face: 6 o'clock plus a long flash = south.

figure.note: Night · six quick flashes, then one long

ru.Night · six quick flashes, then one long: Ночь · шесть частых проблесков, затем длительный

q: At night you see these lights ahead and no others. What is it?
answer: A sailing vessel under sail (red over green masthead lights optional)
why: Red over green at the masthead plus sidelights is a sailing vessel.

q: You see a single steady white light low down, its bearing slowly changing. What is most likely?
answer: The sternlight of a vessel moving away — or an anchored vessel; watch the bearing
why: One white light: stern view or at anchor; only the bearing tells you which.

figure.note: Night · steady white light, bearing drawing slowly left

ru.Night · steady white light, bearing draw: Ночь · постоянный белый огонь, пеленг уходит влево

q: At night you see these lights. What vessel, and who gives way?
answer: A trawler — green over white; you keep clear under sail or power
why: Green over white = trawling; fishing has priority over sail.

q: You are switching from sail to engine at night. Which lights do you turn on and off?
answer: Off: tricolour. On: steaming light plus deck-level sidelights and sternlight
why: Tricolour is for sail only; never with the steaming light.

figure.note: Yacht under sail — about to start the engine

ru.Yacht under sail — about to start the en: Яхта под парусом — сейчас заведёт мотор

q: You are on watch with the skipper asleep below. What do you do?
answer: Wake the skipper now
why: A steady bearing means risk of collision: call the skipper early, never late.

figure.note: Seen for 5 minutes · bearing steady

q: You are approaching this harbour at night. What does the scene mean for your speed?
answer: Slow down — shore lights hide other vessels
why: Rule 6: background light is a factor in choosing a safe speed.

figure.note: Night · harbour entrance against the town lights

ru.Night · harbour entrance against the tow: Ночь · вход в гавань на фоне огней города

q: Motoring at night, this is the only light ahead and you are gaining on it. What do you do?
answer: Keep clear — you are coming up from astern
why: Rule 13: seeing only her sternlight, you are overtaking and keep clear.

figure.note: Night · fine ahead, range closing

ru.Night · fine ahead, range closing: Ночь · почти по носу, дистанция падает

q: Looking astern at night, you see these lights closing on you. What do you do?
answer: Hold course and speed and watch her
why: Rules 13 and 17: a vessel coming up from astern is overtaking; you stand on.

figure.note: Night · dead astern of you, closing fast

ru.Night · dead astern of you, closing fast: Ночь · прямо за кормой, быстро приближается

q: Motoring at night, these lights appear fine ahead on a steady bearing. What do you do?
answer: Alter course to starboard
why: Rule 14: masthead lights in line and both sidelights = head-on; both turn to starboard.

figure.note: Night · fine ahead, bearing steady

ru.Night · fine ahead, bearing steady: Ночь · почти по носу, пеленг не меняется

q: This vessel is nearly ahead and her red light comes and goes. What do you do?
answer: Treat it as head-on and alter to starboard
why: Rule 14(c): if in doubt whether it is head-on, assume it is and act.

figure.note: Night · fine on your starboard bow, closing

ru.Night · fine on your starboard bow, clos: Ночь · чуть справа по носу, сближается

q: You are motoring. These lights are on your port bow on a steady bearing. Your action?
answer: Hold course and speed, ready to act
why: Rules 15 and 17: you see her green, so she has you to starboard and gives way.

figure.note: Night · port bow, bearing steady

ru.Night · port bow, bearing steady: Ночь · слева по носу, пеленг не меняется

q: Motoring at night, you see these lights. Where do you pass?
answer: Well astern of the tow, never between
why: Three masthead lights: a tow over 200 m long, behind the tug — never cut between.

figure.note: Night · starboard bow, bearing steady

ru.Night · starboard bow, bearing steady: Ночь · справа по носу, пеленг не меняется

q: Motoring at night, you see only these two lights, close together, on a steady bearing. What do you do?
answer: Keep clear — she is a yacht under sail
why: No masthead light: a sailing vessel; power keeps clear of sail (Rule 18).

figure.note: Night · starboard bow, bearing steady

ru.Night · starboard bow, bearing steady: Ночь · справа по носу, пеленг не меняется

q: You are under sail alone and see these lights on a steady bearing. What do you do?
answer: Hold course and speed, watching her closely
why: Masthead light and red = power vessel crossing; she keeps clear of sail (Rule 18).

figure.note: Night · on your starboard bow

q: Under sail at night, you see these lights converging. Who keeps clear?
answer: You — she is restricted in manoeuvre
why: Red-white-red all-round = restricted in ability to manoeuvre; sail keeps clear.

figure.note: Night · on your port bow

q: You must pass this fishing vessel. Which side do you choose?
answer: The right-hand side, away from the extra white
why: Rule 26(c): an extra all-round white shows the direction of outlying gear.

figure.note: Night · ahead, not making way

q: You have not yet altered for this ship. She flashes a white light five times, rapidly. What does she mean?
answer: She doubts you are keeping clear — act now
why: Rule 34(d): five short, rapid flashes = doubt; give way clearly now.

figure.note: Night · starboard bow, bearing steady

ru.Night · starboard bow, bearing steady: Ночь · справа по носу, пеленг не меняется

q: This ship flashes her all-round white light twice. What is she doing?
answer: Altering her course to port
why: Rule 34(b): two flashes, like two short blasts = altering to port.

figure.note: Night · on your port bow

q: Approaching on a leading line at night, you see the two lights like this. Which way do you alter?
answer: To starboard, until they line up
why: Move towards the front light: rear showing left of front means you are left of the line.

figure.note: Night · leading lights ahead

q: Entering Kos harbour at night, you see this light ahead, low on the water. On which side do you leave it?
answer: On your starboard side
why: Region A: a green light is a starboard-hand mark; keep it to starboard going in.

figure.note: Night · entering from seaward

q: Near the entrance to Fethiye at night, you see this light low on the water. What is it?
answer: A port-hand lateral mark
why: A red light of any rhythm except Fl(2+1) is a port-hand mark; isolated danger is white Fl(2).

figure.note: Night · light low on the water

q: Coming in from sea, this light marks a fork in the channel. What does it tell you?
answer: Preferred channel to port: leave it to starboard
why: Region A: Fl(2+1) G is a modified starboard-hand mark, so the main channel is to port.

figure.note: Night · channel junction, entering from sea

ru.Night · channel junction, entering from: Ночь · развилка фарватера, вход с моря

q: Entering harbour at night, you have this light fine on your starboard bow. What do you do?
answer: Alter to starboard and leave it to port
why: Region A: a red light is a port-hand mark, so going in it must pass down your port side.

figure.note: Night · entering from sea · light fine to starboard

ru.Night · entering from sea · light fine t: Ночь · вход с моря · огонь чуть справа по носу

q: On the way into a marina at night, you see this light. What is it?
answer: A starboard-hand lateral mark
why: Quick flashing is not only for cardinals: the colour decides, and green is starboard-hand in region A.

figure.note: Night · channel into the marina

q: At night you see this light low on the water ahead. Which side of it is safe?
answer: The east side
why: Three quick flashes = 3 o'clock = east cardinal.

figure.note: Night · light low on the water

q: Approaching the Kornati islands at night, you see this light marking a shoal. Where do you pass it?
answer: To the north
why: Uninterrupted quick or very quick flashing: north cardinal.

figure.note: Night · continuous, about two flashes a second

ru.Night · continuous, about two flashes a: Ночь · непрерывно, около двух проблесков в секунду

q: You time this light on a buoy off Paros. Where do you pass it?
answer: To the west
why: Nine quick flashes = 9 o'clock = west cardinal.

q: At night this light marks a rock in the middle of a bay. What is it?
answer: An isolated danger mark: pass well clear, any side
why: White Fl(2): isolated danger, with navigable water all round.

figure.note: Night · light on a beacon in the bay

ru.Night · light on a beacon in the bay: Ночь · огонь на знаке в бухте

q: Making landfall at night, you see this light ahead, low on the water, alone in open sea. What is it?
answer: A safe water mark
why: White Iso, Oc, LFl 10s or Mo(A): safe water — landfall or mid-channel.

figure.note: Night · approaching from offshore

q: Entering a quiet bay in the Gulf of Corinth at night, you see several of these lights in a rough square. What are they most likely marking?
answer: A fish farm: keep outside them
why: Yellow lights are special marks; in Greek and Turkish bays they often mark fish farms.

figure.note: Night · four lights, low on the water

q: At night you see this light, low on the water, where your chart shows nothing. What is it?
answer: An emergency wreck-marking buoy
why: Alternating blue and yellow flashes: emergency wreck-marking buoy; treat it as a new danger.

figure.note: Night · one light: blue, then yellow, then blue…

ru.Night · one light: blue, then yellow, th: Ночь · один огонь: синий, потом жёлтый, потом синий…

q: Which chart abbreviation matches the harbour light your crew is timing?
answer: Iso 6s
why: Iso = equal light and dark; the period is the whole cycle, 3 + 3 = 6 s.

q: You are coming in on these leading lights and they look like this. Which way do you steer to get back on the line?
answer: To port
why: Move towards the side the front (lower) light has moved to: front left of rear, so go left.

figure.note: Night · leading lights into the harbour

ru.Night · leading lights into the harbour: Ночь · створные огни входа в гавань

q: Approaching a Greek harbour at night, you see these two lights on the breakwater ends. What do you do?
answer: Enter between them, green to starboard
why: Region A: red marks the port side and green the starboard side of the entrance.

figure.note: Night · harbour entrance ahead

q: How is this light written on the chart?
why: Group flashing, two flashes; the period runs from the start of one group to the start of the next.

q: Sailing along the coast at night, the lighthouse you are watching changes colour. What has happened?
answer: You have crossed into its red sector
why: Sectored light: the colour depends on your bearing; red sectors usually cover a danger.

figure.note: Night · white for the last hour, now red

ru.Night · white for the last hour, now red: Ночь · час был белым, теперь красный

q: Motoring at night, you see these lights ahead. What are you looking at?
answer: A power-driven vessel heading towards you
why: A masthead light over both sidelights: power-driven, bow on.

q: What is this vessel, and which side of her are you seeing?
answer: Power-driven; her port side
why: A white masthead light with a red sidelight: power-driven, port side towards you.

q: What do these lights tell you?
answer: A large power vessel showing her starboard side
why: Two masthead lights, the aft one higher, and a green sidelight: big ship, starboard side on.

q: This light is moving slowly from left to right across your bow. What is it?
answer: A sailing vessel showing her starboard side
why: A sidelight with no masthead light above it: a vessel under sail.

figure.note: Night · steady light, no white above it

ru.Night · steady light, no white above it: Ночь · постоянный огонь, белого над ним нет

q: Close inshore at night, you see only this light, moving slowly from right to left. What is it?
answer: A yacht under sail with a tricolour
why: A red sector high at the masthead: the tricolour of a sailing vessel under 20 m, port side on.

figure.note: Night · single steady red light, high up

ru.Night · single steady red light, high up: Ночь · один постоянный красный огонь, высоко

q: These lights are coming towards you. What is it?
answer: A yacht under sail, bow on
why: Green and red together at the masthead with no white: a tricolour seen from ahead.

figure.note: Night · high up, close together, no white light

ru.Night · high up, close together, no whit: Ночь · высоко, рядом, без белого огня

q: Through binoculars you see a yacht with her sails set, showing these lights. What is she under the rules?
answer: A power-driven vessel
why: A steaming light means the engine is running: motor-sailing counts as power-driven.

figure.note: Night · yacht with sails up

q: In the anchorage off Piraeus you see these lights. What is the ship doing, and which way does she lie?
answer: At anchor, bow to the left
why: Rule 30: the forward anchor light is the higher one; under way, the forward masthead light is the lower.

figure.note: Night · deck lights on, no sidelights

ru.Night · deck lights on, no sidelights: Ночь · палубное освещение включено, бортовых нет

q: Off a reef in the Dodecanese you see these lights. What do they tell you?
answer: A vessel aground
why: Two all-round reds plus anchor lights: a vessel aground.

q: What is this vessel?
answer: Not under command, making way
why: Two all-round reds with sidelights and no masthead light: NUC, moving through the water.

q: In open water you see only these lights. What is the vessel doing?
answer: Not under command, stopped in the water
why: NUC shows sidelights only when making way; aground she would add anchor lights.

figure.note: Night · no other lights

q: Crossing the Saronic Gulf at night, you see these lights. What is the vessel?
answer: Restricted in her ability to manoeuvre, under way
why: Red-white-red all-round plus masthead light and sidelights: RAM, making way.

q: These lights belong to a ship off Rhodes. What is her status?
answer: Restricted in ability to manoeuvre, at anchor
why: Red-white-red with an anchor light and no sidelights: RAM at anchor.

figure.note: Night · no sidelights

q: A dredger is working in the channel into Lefkas. On which side can you pass her?
answer: On the side with the two green lights
why: Rule 27(d): two reds mark the obstructed side, two greens the side where you may pass.

q: About a mile off you see these lights and no others. What is the vessel?
answer: A trawler, not making way
why: Green over white = trawling; no sidelights means she is not making way.

figure.note: Night · no sidelights

q: Off Kalymnos at night, a boat shows these lights. What is she?
answer: Fishing (not trawling), making way
why: Red over white: fishing other than trawling; the sidelight shows she is making way.

q: This fishing boat off Sifnos is not making way. Where is her gear?
answer: Out towards the lower white light
why: Rule 26(c): gear out more than 150 m is shown by an all-round white light towards it.

q: Coming up astern of a vessel at night, you see these lights. What is she doing?
answer: Towing
why: A yellow towing light above the sternlight: a vessel towing.

q: What do these lights tell you about the vessel and what is behind her?
answer: She is towing, and the tow is over 200 m
why: Three masthead lights in a vertical line: towing, with a tow longer than 200 m.

q: The tug on the left shows a tow of over 200 m. What must you assume the lone red light on the right is?
answer: The tow: do not cross between them
why: A towed vessel shows only sidelights and sternlight; the tow line lies between it and the tug.

figure.note: Night · the right-hand light is about 400 m astern of the tug

ru.Night · the right-hand light is about 40: Ночь · правый огонь примерно в 400 м за кормой буксировщика

q: A boat is heading for a ship waiting outside the port of Piraeus. These are its lights. What is it?
answer: A pilot vessel on duty, under way
why: White over red: pilot on duty ("white hat, red nose"); the sidelight shows she is under way.

q: A loaded tanker is approaching Agioi Theodoroi at night with these lights. What is she showing?
answer: Constrained by her draught
why: Three all-round reds in a vertical line, plus power-driven lights: constrained by draught.

q: A naval vessel shows these lights. How close may you approach?
answer: No closer than 1000 m
why: Three all-round greens: mine clearance; it is dangerous to come within 1000 m.

q: Far out at sea you first see the white light alone; about ten minutes later the red appears below it. What was the white light?
answer: The masthead light of a power vessel
why: Masthead lights carry 5–6 M, sidelights only 2–3 M, so the masthead light shows first.

q: A minute ago this vessel showed both sidelights. What has she just done?
answer: Altered course to her port
why: Bow on she showed red and green; now only green, so her bow has swung to her port (your right).
